Raspberry Pi 5 storage and cooling guide

The Raspberry Pi 5 is a single-board computer built around the Broadcom BCM2712 quad-core Arm Cortex-A76 processor running at 2.4 GHz. It supports booting from NVMe storage through the PCIe 2.0 interface when an M.2 HAT is attached.

An NVMe SSD is a solid-state drive that communicates over the PCI Express bus instead of SATA. According to our benchmarks, an NVMe drive on the Raspberry Pi 5 achieves sequential reads of about 800 MB/s in PCIe Gen 2 mode.

The board requires a 5V 5A USB-C power supply to deliver full current to USB peripherals. Active cooling is recommended for sustained workloads because the processor throttles at 85 degrees Celsius.

However, PCIe Gen 3 mode is not officially supported and may cause instability on some drives.

Enable NVMe boot

  1. Install the latest bootloader with rpi-eeprom-update.
  2. Set BOOT_ORDER to prefer NVMe in the EEPROM configuration.
  3. Reboot the board and verify the drive with lsblk.
